title: Structured output fallback modes, error semantics, and acceptance test cases
creator: Priya Desai
description: Define clear acceptance criteria and executable test cases for structured-output behaviors when invoking tools/function-calls across streaming and non-streaming responses. Covers schema negotiation, partial emissions, deterministic rollbacks, and fallback routing to compatible model variants.
background: Recent incidents surfaced two classes of failures: (1) streaming responses that emitted partial JSON frames causing downstream tool mis-parses; (2) function-calls that were retried after transient failures and caused duplicate side-effects. There are many existing PM tickets focused on schema negotiation and checkpointing, but we lack a concise acceptance spec and an executable test-suite that QA/Eng can use to validate runtime-2.4 behavior.
scope: Acceptance criteria for structured-output envelopes produced by hosted and dedicated runtimes
Function/tool-calling semantics: handshake, idempotency, and observable fallbacks
Streaming scenarios: partial frames, checkpointed commits, and backpressure-induced truncation
Test cases and telemetry signals that indicate regressions
Pre-release validation harness for integration tests (QA + CI)
out_of_scope: New SDK surface design (separate DES/ENG tickets)
Long-term model-evolution policies beyond immediate fallback rules
On-prem upgrade automation for legacy agent versions
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Deterministic envelope schema - Every emitted structured payload MUST start with a single opening envelope token ("envelope_start") and end with a closing token ("envelope_commit") within a 30s window for non-streaming and within the stream's TTL for streaming responses.

AC-2: Progressive validation levels - The runtime MUST expose validation_level metadata (none|schema-lite|schema-strict). For schema-lite, runtime tolerates unknown fields; for schema-strict, unknown fields must be emitted as validation_warnings and not sent to tools unless acknowledged.

AC-3: Idempotent function-calls - For any tool/function invocation the runtime MUST include an idempotency_token in the call envelope. If a transient retry occurs, downstream systems MUST see at most one effective execution when the tool honors token semantics. Acceptance tests will simulate a double-delivery with identical token and expect a single side-effect recorded.

AC-4: Partial-frame recovery - If a stream connection is interrupted mid-frame, the runtime MUST provide a checkpoint anchor (checkpoint_id) for the last fully-committed fragment. Consumers must be able to resume using checkpoint_id and receive the remainder of the payload without re-processing committed fragments.

AC-5: Graceful schema mismatch fallback - When the emitted schema does not match the consumer's required schema and schema-strict is requested, the runtime MUST: (a) stop broadcast to tools, (b) emit a structured error frame with a recovery_suggestion, and (c) route the request to the fallback model variant if configured within fallback_policy timeout.

AC-6: Explicit error classification - All structured error frames MUST include error_class (transient|recoverable|fatal), error_code, human_readable_message, and suggested_action (retry|fallback|abort). Telemetry must map these to SLO-impacting alerts.

AC-7: Backpressure semantics - When downstream tooling signals backpressure, streaming responses MUST: (a) buffer up to configured buffer_limit per-client, (b) apply incremental checkpoint commits at safe boundaries, and (c) if buffer_limit exceeded, emit a backpressure_truncated frame with clear guidance for resumption or cancellation.

AC-8: Observability and traces - Every function-call lifecycle (handshake -> invocation -> commit/rollback) MUST emit a trace/span with ids cross-linkable to request_id and model_variant. Console must display these within per-route traces within 5s of event completion.

AC-9: Test harness determinism - Integration tests for acceptance MUST be deterministic under controlled network jitter and rely on injected timeouts rather than wall-clock metrics. Tests failing intermittently will be considered not yet accepted.

AC-10: Backward compatibility opt-in - Customers who opt-in to legacy_schema_mode must receive a best-effort compatibility shim, and acceptance tests MUST include a compatibility matrix validating legacy->new schema mappings for representative payloads.
test_cases: TC-01: Double-delivery idempotency test - Send a function-call with idempotency_token X; interrupt network after gateway forwards; simulate re-send with same token; assert tool recorded one execution and runtime emitted duplicate_suppressed event.

TC-02: Partial-frame resume - Start a streaming structured response, cut connection at random byte between fragments; resume using checkpoint_id; confirm consumer receives missing fragments exactly once and final envelope_commit.

TC-03: Schema-strict rejection - Set consumer to schema-strict; emit payload with extra unexpected required field; expect runtime to emit structured_error with error_class=fatal and suggested_action=abort; ensure no tool invocation occurred.

TC-04: Schema-lite tolerant path - Same payload as TC-03 but validation_level=schema-lite; expect runtime to emit validation_warnings and forward permitted fields to tool; warnings are recorded in trace.

TC-05: Backpressure truncation - Configure buffer_limit=32KB; stream a large structured payload; have downstream signal backpressure; expect checkpointed commits at 8KB boundaries and eventual backpressure_truncated with resume tokens.

TC-06: Fallback routing on timeout - Configure fallback_policy to switch to model-compat within 2s; induce slow model variant; verify request routed to fallback variant and telemetry shows fallback_reason=latency_threshold_exceeded.

TC-07: Observability end-to-end - For a full function-call sequence, validate that Console shows request_id, idempotency_token, trace spans, and error frames within 5s and that token-level cost breakdowns correlate to emitted tokens.
TC-08: Deterministic test under jitter - Run TC-02 with synthetic jitter in CI; acceptance requires zero flaky runs across 20 iterations.
TC-09: Unauthorized tool invocation - Simulate missing tool scope in token; expect structured_error with error_class=recoverable, suggested_action=abort, and no tool side-effects.
success_metrics: 0 flaky failures across 20 CI runs for deterministic acceptance tests
<0.1% production events with malformed envelope_start/envelope_commit in first 30 days post-release
Idempotency deduplication rate >= 99.9% for retried invocations in synthetic load tests
Mean time to surface structured_error events in Console < 10s
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime-2.4 change with feature-flag gated structured_envelope_v2
2) Deploy to canary hosts in hosted-region-us-west with telemetry hooks enabled
3) Run full TC suite against canary for 48h, validate success_metrics
4) Gradual rollout to 25% capacity with opt-in customers allowed to use legacy_schema_mode
5) Full rollout after 7 days if no P0 regressions and acceptance tests stable
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Chose checkpoint_id approach instead of re-streaming from token offsets to simplify consumer resumption logic (PM + Eng consensus).
2025-02-18: Agreed on three validation_levels (none|schema-lite|schema-strict). Design sign-off by Design on 2025-02-19.
2025-02-24: Idempotency_token made mandatory for all function-calls in streaming paths to prevent duplicate side-effects.
